beats.intent: ThinkSR carries a low-resolution image through encoding, windowing, shared recurrent DQ-CTM ticks, and decoding.
beats.claim: ThinkSR end to end: encoder, windows, shared DQ-CTM ticks, decoder.
beats.narration: The method keeps a dense carrier so super-resolution still has spatial detail to reconstruct. The encoder turns the low-resolution input into features. Windowing partitions those features for local processing. The DQ-CTM thought process runs repeated ticks with shared parameters. The decoder turns the updated dense field back into a high-resolution image.

params.headline: ThinkSR runs dense features through shared thought ticks.
params.note: Parameters are shared across DQ-CTM ticks.

beats.intent: The encoder creates the dense carrier, and the window partition preserves every token from that carrier.
beats.narration: The carrier is defined before the compact thought process starts. The encoder maps the low-resolution image into the dense feature field. The window partition takes that field as input and keeps every token for processing.

params.headline: The carrier equation makes dense features before windows.

beats.intent: DQ-CTM-SR is not the smallest model; at 1.129 million parameters, it is the second largest of the five compared methods.
beats.claim: Table 1 — ×4 lightweight super-resolution, average over five benchmarks.
beats.narration: Parameter count shows that the proposed model is not the cheap option in this comparison. CATANet is the smallest at 0.535 million parameters. RFDN is nearly the same size at 0.550 million. IMDN is larger at 0.715 million. DQ-CTM-SR is second largest at 1.129 million. CARN is largest at 1.592 million.

params.headline: DQ-CTM-SR is the second largest model compared.
params.note: Smallest first; DQ-CTM-SR is second largest.
